Implemented + deployed via rockymtn (nixos-rebuild switch, granite pinned at 4b4985b/67deb70).

Ported Omarchy's persistence layer, reduced to granite's entry shape:
- one JSON file per on-screen popup under
  ~/.local/state/granite/notifications/, moved into history/ when the
  toast leaves the screen (any reason); that directory IS the history
  (in-memory array removed)
- images/ copies of file-backed images (Chromium-family senders delete
  originals on close), each copy keyed to its JSON file stem
- startup restore: expired entries archive, survivors re-show with a
  full lifetime persisted as an absolute deadline; orphan image sweep
- serialized job queue for writes/moves/deletes; DND-silenced writes
  hold tracked until file+copies are on disk (replaces_id catch-up)
- showHistory replays history/ through a barrier read, carrying
  on-screen rows over in memory; clearHistory wipes dir + images

Verified live on mikes-desktop: toast -> file -> shell restart ->
restored with deadline -> expiry archives to history/ -> showHistory
replays -> clearHistory wipes. JS helpers + bash job scripts
unit-tested; full QML integration-tested offscreen (restore, sweep,
archive, deadline-across-second-restart, IPC round-trip).
